question: What is the geometric meaning of an eigenvector?
direct_answer: It is a direction that a linear transformation does not rotate away from itself.
expanded_answer: An eigenvector marks a direction that stays on the same line after the transformation. The vector may get longer, shorter, or reversed, but its direction is preserved up to sign.
key_points: Only magnitude or orientation along the line may change
common_wrong_ideas: Believing the vector must stay exactly unchanged
Assuming every transformation has obvious real eigenvectors
